claim.pdf_says: 13.17.3   Syntax rules — printed at the same heading depth as 13.17.1 General, 13.17.2 General formats and 13.17.4 General rules (all three-component subclause numbers under 13.17).
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 17201: "## 13.17.3 Syntax rules" — an H2, while its siblings are H3: line 17051 "### 13.17.1 General", line 17056 "### 13.17.2 General formats", line 17254 "### 13.17.4 General rules", under line 17048 "## 13.17 Screen description entry".
claim.why_it_matters: 13.17.3 is promoted a level, so it renders as a peer of clause 13.17 itself rather than as one of its subclauses. Any generated table of contents, anchor map, or section-extraction tool that walks heading depth will place the Syntax rules of the screen description entry outside 13.17, breaking §-citation lookups for exactly the rules a compiler needs (e.g. 13.17.3 SR 1 on entry-name-clause ordering).

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED on the facts, with the label and the impact both overstated. (1) Both quotes are exact. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 17048 '## 13.17 Screen description entry', 17051 '### 13.17.1 General', 17056 '### 13.17.2 General formats', 17201 '## 13.17.3 Syntax rules', 17254 '### 13.17.4 General rules'. So 13.17.3 is an H2 sitting at the same markdown depth as its own parent clause, while all three of its siblings are H3. (2) Independent PDF confirmation of the intended depth did NOT come from the printed page. I rendered spec_p400.png and read it: the heading '13.17.3 Syntax rules' appears near the foot of the page above 'ALL FORMATS'. PyMuPDF span metadata for pages 398-401 shows EVERY heading — 13.17 (p398 y=90.2), 13.17.1 (p398 y=115.5), 13.17.2 (p398 y=204.0), 13.17.3 (p400 y=556.2), 13.17.4 (p401 y=558.1) — set in Cambria,Bold at 11.67 pt, so the print gives no type-size cue to depth at all. The authoritative signal is the PDF's own embedded bookmark outline (2090 entries, titles are not obfuscated even though the body text layer is): it records '13.17 Screen description entry' at level=2 and '13.17.1 General', '13.17.2 General formats', '13.17.3 Syntax rules', '13.17.4 General rules' all at level=3. The markdown therefore contradicts the PDF's own recorded hierarchy for 13.17.3, and the surrounding markdown (13.17 -> H2, 13.17.1 -> H3) proves the file's own convention is md-depth == outline-level. (3) Not page-break furniture, not reflow, not hyphenation: no text is lost or moved. (4) Rejected sub-claims. The kind label 'missing-heading' is wrong — nothing is missing. The heading number, the heading text, and the '' anchor immediately above line 17201 are all present and correct, and the transcribed contents list at line 657 links '[13.17.3 Syntax rules](#section-13-17-3) ... [370](#page-370)' correctly. So §-citation lookup by clause number or by anchor is NOT broken; only a consumer that infers hierarchy from '#' count is affected, and that consumer is already unreliable on this file because every page break emits an H2 '## Page NNN' (e.g. line 2 of the page-400 slice) interleaved with the clause tree. (5) The decisive correction is scale. I diffed every numbered markdown heading against the PDF outline level: 333 agree, 1391 disagree, of which 1334 are markdown depths SHALLOWER than the outline level. 13.17.3 is not an isolated defect but one instance of a systematic transcription bug in which the first subclause of a group keeps its depth and later siblings are promoted — 13.16.2 / 13.16.3 / 13.16.4 are H2-vs-level-3 exactly like 13.17.3, and the entire run 13.18.2 through 13.18.64 plus all of their .1/.2/.3/.4 children is shifted the same way. Filing this as a per-page structural finding is accurate but near-worthless in isolation; the fix is one mechanical pass that re-derives every clause heading depth from the PDF's embedded outline.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a missing heading — a heading-DEPTH error, and a document-wide one. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 17201 writes '## 13.17.3 Syntax rules' (H2) where the PDF's embedded bookmark outline records '13.17.3 Syntax rules' at level 3, alongside 13.17.1 / 13.17.2 / 13.17.4 (level 3) under 13.17 Screen description entry (level 2); the markdown's own siblings at lines 17051 / 17056 / 17254 are correctly H3, so the file contradicts itself. The printed page carries no type-size cue — 13.17 through 13.17.4 are all Cambria,Bold 11.67 pt — so depth comes from the clause number and the outline, not the glyphs. Impact is narrower than claimed: the '' anchor and the contents entry at line 657 are both correct, so §-citation lookup still resolves; only heading-depth-walking tools misplace the clause, and those are already confounded by the '## Page NNN' H2 page markers. Scope is far wider than claimed: 1334 numbered headings across the file sit shallower than their PDF outline level (13.16.2/.3/.4 and the whole 13.18.2–13.18.64 run behave identically), so this should be closed by one mechanical re-derivation of heading depth from the PDF outline, not by a one-line edit at 17201.
